summary:
Since 2000, NASA satellites have recorded fire hotspots, published through NASA FIRMS. The record is split between two instruments: MODIS (2000 onward, 1 km pixels) and VIIRS (2012 onward, 375 m pixels). VIIRS sees smaller fires and records 3.5 to 4.6 times more hotspots, so the record shows 2012 as the year fires multiplied. With MODIS near its end and Suomi NPP stopped on 2 November 2026, analysts lose the answer to their monthly question: is this month’s fire activity normal for this area?

We built a harmonized fire activity calendar from 7.4 million FIRMS hotspots from five satellites over Italy and Argentina. Instead of counting hotspots, we rebuild every satellite pass, spread each pixel’s real footprint over hexagons of about 36 km², and count the hexagons above 0.5 MW/km², where both instruments agree. One satellite per month, with a single small factor, joins 2000 to today into one series.

Tested on 2012-2025, when both instruments flew, our series gives the same verdict as MODIS alone in 82% of months in Italy and 96% in Argentina. The web app, for fire analysts and scientists, shows the verdict, the calendar, the map and downloadable data, updated from FIRMS every three hours.
details:
NASA FIRMS has mapped fire hotspots since 2000 with MODIS (1 km pixels) and, since 2012, VIIRS (375 m), which records 5-7 times more. Joined as they are, 2012 looks like the year fires multiplied, so 25 years of data cannot tell analysts whether this month's fire activity is normal.

We built the method on 7.4 million hotspots over Italy and Argentina, then ran it on every country. No single factor fixes counts, so we changed the unit: each pixel's real footprint is spread over H3 hexagons of about 36 km² as fire power per km². A hexagon is active at 0.5 MW/km² or more, where both sensors agree. We count active hexagons per area and month, read one satellite per month and bring VIIRS to the MODIS scale with each country's own factor.

The web app opens on a globe of 230 countries, each with a harmonized calendar from 2000 and a verdict: above, within or below the usual, or "we can't tell". Italy and Argentina add regional maps, weather, likely fire causes, downloads, a data assistant and a FIRMS refresh every 3 hours. For Argentina it continues the SNMF report after Suomi NPP stopped on 2 November 2026.

Over 2012-2025, when both flew, we match MODIS verdicts in 82% of months in Italy and 96% in Argentina; the largest jump at a satellite change is 9%. Spain, never used to build the method, stays within 1% of Aqua; 82 countries land within 10% in 82% of country-years.

As MODIS nears its end, fire analysts and scientists keep a record comparable from 2000 to today.
dataRefs: FIRMS, MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m active fires (S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21): the hotspots we harmonize into one monthly series, from November 2000 to today.
GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services): dated satellite imagery and MODIS and VIIRS fire layers under the hotspots in the app.
Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS): 30 m images before and after a fire.
LIS/OTD lightning climatology, GHRC DAAC: lightning in the index of who lights the fires.
SEDAC Gridded Population of the World v4.11: population near the fires.
NASA POWER: monthly weather per region in the first analysis.
NASA 3D Resources: the Terra and Suomi NPP satellites in the demo video, no NASA logos.
Full list: every data source, with licence, on the project site; papers, media and the other resources in its References section.
projectRefs: CONAE (Argentina), user manual of the MODIS/VIIRS hotspot viewer: how the Argentine operational system already combines the two sensors.
ERA5, Copernicus Climate Data Store (ECMWF): the weather of each month, compared with 2001-2025.
Fire Weather Index, Copernicus Emergency Management Service: fire danger of each month.
ESA CCI Land Cover: crop, forest, shrub and grass around the fires.
Fire cause records of Spain (EGIF), Canada (NFDB) and the United States (WFIGS), road density (GRIP4) and crop calendars (SAGE): ground truth and predictors of who lights the fires.
Boundaries (ISTAT via openpolis, IGN Argentina via Georef, Natural Earth) and basemaps (CARTO, OpenStreetMap, Sentinel-2 cloudless by EOX): the areas of the fire calendar and the maps.
Full list: every data source and reference, with licence, on the project site.
